database_info.title: Master's Level Comprehensive Symptoms Database
database_info.purpose: Academic medical reference for symptom assessment and treatment guidance

symptoms.description: Elevated body temperature above normal range (>37.5°C/99.5°F)

mild.characteristics: Minimal discomfort, able to function normally

moderate.characteristics: Notable discomfort, some activity limitation, malaise

severe.characteristics: Significant impairment, risk of complications, severe discomfort

home_remedies: Rest adequately - 8-10 hours of sleep
Increase fluid intake to 2-3 liters/day (water, clear broths, electrolyte solutions)
Apply cool compress to forehead, neck, and wrists
Wear light, breathable clothing
Maintain room temperature at 20-22°C (68-72°F)
Lukewarm bath (not cold) if fever very high
Avoid bundling up - allows heat dissipation

otc_medications.notes: First-line antipyretic, hepatotoxic in overdose, safe for most patients
NSAID with anti-inflammatory properties, take with food
otc_medications.contraindications: Peptic ulcer, kidney disease, pregnancy (3rd trimester), bleeding disorders

otc_medications.notes: Effective antipyretic, NOT for children <16 due to Reye's syndrome risk

red_flags: Severe headache with neck stiffness (meningitis concern)
Altered mental status, confusion, or lethargy
Persistent vomiting or inability to keep fluids down

emergency_911: Signs of meningitis (stiff neck, severe headache, photophobia, rash)
primary_care_24_48hrs: Fever with localized symptoms (ear pain, sore throat)

key_points: Fever is a symptom, not a disease - it indicates body's immune response
Goal is patient comfort, not necessarily achieving normal temperature
Alternating acetaminophen and ibuprofen not routinely recommended
Monitor hydration status - urine should be pale yellow
Keep temperature log if fever persists
Fever in children is common and usually benign if child is well-appearing

symptoms.description: Sudden, forceful expulsion of air from lungs

mild.characteristics: No interference with sleep or daily activities, no sputum production

moderate.characteristics: Affects sleep quality, some activity limitation, may have sputum

severe.characteristics: Significant sleep disruption, breathlessness, hemoptysis, chest pain

cough_types.dry_cough: Non-productive, irritating, often viral or allergic

home_remedies: Honey: 1-2 teaspoons before bed (proven effective for cough suppression) - NOT for infants <1 year
Hydration: Warm liquids (tea, broth) help thin secretions
Humidifier: Add moisture to air, especially during sleep
Steam inhalation: 10-15 minutes, 2-3 times daily
Elevate head while sleeping (30-45 degrees)
Avoid irritants: smoke, strong perfumes, cold air
Throat lozenges or hard candy (for adults)
Ginger tea with honey
Saltwater gargle for throat irritation

otc_medications.dosage: Adults: 10-20mg every 4 hours or 60mg extended-release every 12 hours (max 120mg/day)
otc_medications.mechanism: Cough suppressant - acts on cough center in brain
otc_medications.best_for: Dry, non-productive cough interfering with sleep
otc_medications.notes: May cause drowsiness, do not use with MAOIs
otc_medications.contraindications: MAOI use, chronic cough, productive cough with excessive secretions

otc_medications.dosage: Adults: 200-400mg every 4 hours or 600-1200mg extended-release every 12 hours
otc_medications.mechanism: Expectorant - helps thin and loosen mucus
otc_medications.notes: Must drink plenty of water for effectiveness

otc_medications.best_for: Nighttime cough from post-nasal drip or allergies
otc_medications.notes: Causes significant drowsiness - bedtime use only
Provides symptomatic relief only

red_flags: Significant weight loss with chronic cough

emergency_911: Coughing up large amounts of blood
urgent_care_same_day: Signs of pneumonia (fever, shortness of breath, chest pain)
primary_care_1_week: Cough interfering significantly with sleep or daily activities

key_points: Cough is protective reflex to clear airways
Antibiotics do NOT help viral coughs (most common cause)
Honey more effective than OTC cough medicines for children >1 year
Cough can persist 3-8 weeks after viral infection (post-viral cough)
Smoking cessation crucial for chronic cough
Stay hydrated to help thin secretions
prevention: Avoid close contact with sick individuals

symptoms.description: Pain or discomfort in head, scalp, or neck region

mild.characteristics: Dull ache, doesn't interfere with activities, responsive to OTC medication

moderate.characteristics: Noticeable impairment, difficulty concentrating, some activity limitation

severe.characteristics: Debilitating, unable to function, may have nausea/vomiting, light/sound sensitivity

headache_types.tension_type: Most common, band-like pressure, bilateral, stress-related
headache_types.migraine: Unilateral, throbbing, with nausea, photophobia, aura possible
headache_types.cluster: Severe unilateral orbital pain, lacrimation, rhinorrhea, rare
headache_types.sinus: Facial pressure, worse with bending, associated with sinus congestion
headache_types.secondary: Due to underlying condition (infection, trauma, etc.)

home_remedies: Rest in quiet, dark room
Apply cold compress to forehead or ice pack to neck (15-20 min)
Apply warm compress to tense neck muscles
Gentle massage of temples, neck, and shoulders
Stay well-hydrated - drink water regularly
Regular sleep schedule (7-9 hours)
Stress reduction: meditation, deep breathing, yoga
Limit screen time - follow 20-20-20 rule (every 20 min, look 20 feet away for 20 sec)
Maintain good posture, especially at desk
Regular meals to prevent hypoglycemia
Peppermint or lavender essential oil to temples
Caffeine in small amounts (if not overused) can help some headaches

otc_medications.notes: First-line for frequent headaches (lower risk of rebound)

otc_medications.efficacy: Very effective for tension headaches and migraines
otc_medications.notes: Take with food, more effective than acetaminophen for inflammation
otc_medications.contraindications: GI ulcers, kidney disease, bleeding disorders

otc_medications.notes: Can be combined with caffeine (Excedrin) for migraine
Caffeine enhances analgesic effect, but can cause dependence
Longer duration than ibuprofen

red_flags: Sudden severe 'thunderclap' headache (worst headache of life)
Headache with fever, stiff neck, and rash (meningitis)
Progressive worsening over days to weeks
New headache in person >50 years old
Headache with neurological symptoms: weakness, numbness, vision changes, speech difficulty
Headache with confusion or altered consciousness
Headache that changes with position (worse lying down)
Headache with jaw claudication or vision loss (temporal arteritis in elderly)
First severe headache in person with cancer or HIV

emergency_911: Thunderclap headache (sudden, severe, peak within seconds)
Headache with paralysis, weakness, or numbness
Headache with severe confusion or difficulty speaking
urgent_care_same_day: Severe headache not responding to usual treatment
Headache with high fever and stiff neck
Sudden onset severe headache (even if improving)
primary_care_1_2_weeks: Medication overuse headache (>15 days/month analgesic use)

key_points: Keep headache diary: track frequency, severity, triggers, medications used
Identify and avoid triggers: stress, certain foods, sleep deprivation
Regular lifestyle: consistent sleep, meals, exercise
Limit caffeine intake and avoid abrupt cessation
Beware medication overuse: using pain medication >2-3 days/week can cause rebound headaches
Proper ergonomics at work and home
Stay hydrated throughout day
migraine_specific: Common triggers: aged cheese, chocolate, alcohol, processed meats, MSG

symptoms.description: Nausea: unpleasant sensation of need to vomit. Vomiting: forceful expulsion of gastric contents

mild.characteristics: Able to keep some fluids down, minimal dehydration risk

moderate.characteristics: Difficulty keeping fluids down, early dehydration signs

severe.characteristics: Unable to keep anything down, significant dehydration, hematemesis

home_remedies: Initial management: Nothing by mouth for 1-2 hours after vomiting
Gradual rehydration: Small sips (1-2 teaspoons) every 5-10 minutes
Clear liquids: water, ice chips, clear broth, diluted apple juice, oral rehydration solution
Ginger: Fresh ginger tea, ginger ale (real ginger), ginger candies - proven antiemetic
Peppermint: Tea or aromatherapy (smell peppermint oil)
BRAT diet: Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast - once tolerating fluids
Acupressure: P6 point on wrist (3 finger-widths below wrist crease)
Fresh air and cool environment
Avoid strong odors, greasy/spicy/fatty foods
Rest in comfortable position (left side may help)
Cold compress on forehead or back of neck
Frequent small meals once improving

otc_medications.dosage: Adults: 524mg (2 tablets) every 30-60 minutes as needed (max 8 doses/24hrs)
otc_medications.best_for: Nausea, upset stomach, diarrhea, food poisoning
otc_medications.notes: Can darken tongue and stool (black) - normal. Contains aspirin-like compound
otc_medications.contraindications: Aspirin allergy, children with viral illness (Reye's syndrome risk), bleeding disorders

otc_medications.notes: Take 30-60 minutes before travel. Causes drowsiness
Take 1 hour before travel, longer acting than dimenhydrinate

otc_medications.dosage: Adults: 15-30mL, repeat every 15 min until distress subsides (max 5 doses/hour)
otc_medications.mechanism: Reduces smooth muscle contraction in GI tract
otc_medications.notes: High sugar content - use caution in diabetes
Essential component of treatment, especially with diarrhea

red_flags: Hematemesis: vomiting blood (red or coffee-ground appearance)
Severe abdominal pain, especially right lower quadrant
Signs of dehydration: dizziness, dark urine, dry mucous membranes, decreased urination
Unable to keep any fluids down for >24 hours (adults) or >12 hours (children)
Severe dehydration signs: lethargy, sunken eyes, no tears, no urine >8 hours

emergency_911: Severe abdominal pain with rigid abdomen
Signs of severe dehydration with altered consciousness
urgent_care_same_day: Unable to keep fluids down >24 hours
Infant or elderly with persistent vomiting
primary_care_24_48hrs: Persistent nausea affecting quality of life

dehydration_assessment.mild: Thirsty, dry lips, decreased urine (darker color)
dehydration_assessment.moderate: Very thirsty, dry mouth, minimal urine, dizziness when standing, fatigue
dehydration_assessment.severe: Extremely thirsty or not thirsty, no urine output, sunken eyes, rapid heartbeat, lethargy, confusion

key_points: Dehydration is main concern with vomiting - focus on fluid replacement
Reintroduce foods gradually - don't rush
Viral gastroenteritis is self-limited (usually 24-72 hours)
Hand hygiene crucial to prevent spread
Antiemetics not always necessary - may prolong viral illness
Monitor urine output and color as hydration indicator
when_rehydrating: Popsicles and ice chips count as fluids
Oral rehydration solution better than plain water (contains electrolytes)

symptoms.description: Loose, watery stools occurring more frequently than normal (>3 per day)

mild.characteristics: Minimal cramping, no blood, able to maintain hydration

moderate.characteristics: Moderate cramping, some dehydration risk, interferes with activities

severe.characteristics: Severe cramping, blood/mucus present, significant dehydration risk, fever

home_remedies: Oral rehydration: Most important - drink 2-3 liters/day minimum
Oral rehydration solution (ORS): Pedialyte, Hydralyte - ideal for electrolyte replacement
BRAT diet: Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast - easy to digest, binding
Additional foods: Plain crackers, boiled potatoes, chicken (no skin), clear broth
Probiotics: Yogurt with live cultures, kefir, or probiotic supplements
Avoid: Dairy (if lactose intolerant), fatty/greasy foods, spicy foods, caffeine, alcohol
Chamomile or peppermint tea: Soothing to GI tract
Rest and let body recover
Maintain hygiene: Frequent handwashing to prevent spread
Small frequent meals rather than large meals

otc_medications.dosage: Adults: 4mg initially, then 2mg after each loose stool (max 8mg/24hrs for OTC, 16mg with MD supervision)
otc_medications.best_for: Non-infectious diarrhea, traveler's diarrhea (if no fever)
otc_medications.notes: Very effective. Do NOT use if fever, bloody stool, or severe abdominal pain
otc_medications.contraindications: Bloody diarrhea, high fever, C. difficile colitis, children <2 years
otc_medications.warning: Can worsen certain infections by preventing toxin clearance

otc_medications.dosage: Adults: 524mg (2 tablets) every 30-60 minutes as needed (max 8 doses/24hrs)
otc_medications.best_for: Traveler's diarrhea, food poisoning, general diarrhea
otc_medications.notes: Can be used WITH loperamide. Will darken tongue/stool (normal)

otc_medications.dosage: Varies by product - follow label, typically 10-20 billion CFU daily
otc_medications.notes: S. boulardii particularly effective for C. diff and antibiotic-associated diarrhea

otc_medications.dosage: Frequent sips throughout day - aim for matching output
otc_medications.notes: Most critical component of treatment. Better than plain water

red_flags: Blood in stool (red blood or black tarry stools)
Unable to keep any fluids down

emergency_911: Severe dehydration with altered mental status
Bloody diarrhea with fever and severe abdominal pain
Signs of shock (rapid pulse, low BP, confusion)
urgent_care_same_day: Elderly, infant, or immunocompromised with diarrhea

key_points: Most acute diarrhea is viral and self-limited (2-7 days)
Hydration is key - drink more than you think you need
Antibiotics usually not needed and can worsen some causes
Antidiarrheals can be harmful if fever or blood present
Hygiene critical: wash hands frequently, disinfect surfaces
Probiotics may shorten duration and aid recovery
prevention: Food safety: cook meat thoroughly, wash produce
Avoid raw/undercooked foods in endemic areas
rehydration_guidance: Drink 8-16 oz after each loose stool
ORS better than sports drinks (better Na:glucose ratio)
Signs you're well-hydrated: pale yellow urine, normal urination frequency
Children need special attention - dehydrate faster

symptoms.description: Uncomfortable sensation of difficulty breathing or inability to get enough air

mild.characteristics: Can speak in full sentences, able to lie flat, normal respiratory rate

moderate.description: Breathlessness with minimal activity or at rest
moderate.characteristics: Difficulty speaking full sentences, prefers sitting upright, increased respiratory rate

severe.characteristics: Unable to speak, gasping for air, cyanosis, altered mental status, respiratory rate >30

home_remedies: Sit upright in comfortable position (forward-leaning may help)
Practice pursed-lip breathing: Inhale through nose (2 counts), exhale slowly through pursed lips (4 counts)
Use fan directed at face for cooling sensation
Stay calm - anxiety worsens breathlessness
Loosen tight clothing around neck/chest
Open window for fresh air circulation
Diaphragmatic breathing exercises
Maintain healthy weight to reduce work of breathing
Avoid triggers: allergens, smoke, pollution
Elevate head with pillows when sleeping
Stay hydrated
Gradual exercise program (after medical clearance)

otc_medications.dosage: 1-2 inhalations, wait 1 minute, may repeat (max 8 inhalations/24hrs)
otc_medications.notes: OTC epinephrine inhaler available but prescription bronchodilators (albuterol) much more effective and safer
otc_medications.warning: If needing frequently, requires medical evaluation

otc_medications.medication: Note: Most causes of dyspnea require prescription treatment
otc_medications.notes: Seek medical evaluation for proper diagnosis and treatment

red_flags: CRITICAL: Sudden severe shortness of breath (CALL 911)
Chest pain with dyspnea (possible MI, PE, pneumothorax)
Inability to speak due to breathlessness
Using accessory muscles to breathe (neck, abdomen)
Recent surgery or prolonged immobility (PE risk)

emergency_911: Chest pain with shortness of breath
Severe asthma attack not responding to inhaler
primary_care_within_week: Need for evaluation of known condition

key_points: Shortness of breath is always a symptom requiring evaluation
Cardiac and pulmonary causes most common
Anxiety can cause dyspnea but is diagnosis of exclusion
Progressive worsening requires urgent evaluation
Learn proper inhaler technique if prescribed
Create asthma action plan if applicable
breathing_techniques: Pursed-lip breathing slows breathing rate and keeps airways open longer
Diaphragmatic breathing more efficient than chest breathing
Practice when well to use during episodes
Sitting upright or leaning forward reduces work of breathing

symptoms.description: Discomfort or pain in chest region - REQUIRES CAREFUL EVALUATION

mild.characteristics: Reproducible with movement, no radiation, short duration

moderate.characteristics: Noticeable pain affecting activities, may radiate, unclear cause

severe.characteristics: Substernal pressure, radiation to arm/jaw, associated symptoms (sweating, nausea), prolonged duration

common_causes: Musculoskeletal (chest wall strain, costochondritis) - most common non-cardiac

home_remedies: FIRST: Rule out cardiac emergency (see red flags)
Rest and avoid strenuous activities
Apply heat or cold to chest wall if musculoskeletal
Practice stress reduction if anxiety-related
Avoid GERD triggers if reflux suspected: spicy/fatty foods, lying down after eating
Maintain good posture
Deep breathing exercises (if not cardiac)
Gentle stretching of chest muscles

otc_medications.notes: ONLY after cardiac causes ruled out. Quick test: if antacids relieve pain, suggests GERD
otc_medications.warning: Do NOT assume chest pain is GERD without evaluation

otc_medications.notes: ONLY after cardiac causes ruled out
otc_medications.contraindications: History of GI bleeding, kidney disease
otc_medications.warning: Do NOT take for cardiac chest pain

otc_medications.dosage: Chew 325mg immediately if heart attack suspected
otc_medications.best_for: SUSPECTED HEART ATTACK while waiting for EMS
otc_medications.notes: Call 911 FIRST, then chew aspirin if no contraindications
otc_medications.warning: Only use if heart attack suspected and no contraindications

red_flags: - Pain radiating to left arm, jaw, neck, or back
- New chest pain in person >40 with cardiac risk factors
- Chest pain with exertion that improves with rest (angina)
- Sudden onset pleuritic pain (worse with breathing)
- Tearing sensation radiating to back (aortic dissection)
- Chest pain with fever and cough (pneumonia)

emergency_911: ANY chest pain with cardiac characteristics
Chest pain with dyspnea, sweating, or radiation
Suspected heart attack, PE, or aortic dissection
Chest pain in known cardiac disease
urgent_care_same_day: Persistent chest discomfort after cardiac causes evaluated
Reproducible chest wall pain needing evaluation
Chest pain in young patient with low cardiac risk

key_points: NEVER ignore chest pain - when in doubt, seek evaluation
Cardiac chest pain is often pressure/heaviness, not sharp
Classic heart attack presentation: substernal pressure radiating to left arm
Women and elderly may have atypical presentations
Time is muscle - early treatment saves heart tissue
Aspirin during heart attack reduces mortality
Most chest pain is not cardiac, but must rule out first
when_to_call_911: Do NOT drive yourself to hospital

symptoms.description: Pain or discomfort in abdominal region between chest and pelvis

mild.characteristics: Able to function, no guarding, tolerating oral intake

moderate.characteristics: Some difficulty with movement, localized tenderness, reduced oral intake

severe.characteristics: Unable to find comfortable position, guarding, rebound tenderness, associated symptoms

home_remedies: Rest in comfortable position
Apply heating pad to abdomen (15-20 min intervals)
Gentle abdominal massage in clockwise direction
Start with clear liquids, progress to bland diet
BRAT diet if tolerated: Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast
Avoid gas-producing foods: beans, cabbage, carbonated drinks
Stay hydrated with small frequent sips
Peppermint or chamomile tea for cramping
Avoid solid foods initially if nausea/vomiting present
Practice stress reduction if stress-related
Knee-to-chest position may relieve gas pain

otc_medications.dosage: Adults: 125-250mg after meals and at bedtime (max 500mg/24hrs)
otc_medications.mechanism: Anti-foaming agent - breaks up gas bubbles
otc_medications.notes: Very safe, works locally in gut, not absorbed systemically

otc_medications.dosage: As directed on package, usually 2-4 tablets as needed
otc_medications.best_for: Upper abdominal pain from indigestion, gastritis, GERD
otc_medications.notes: Provides rapid relief for acid-related pain

otc_medications.dosage: Adults: 524mg (2 tablets) every 30-60 min as needed (max 8 doses/24hrs)
otc_medications.best_for: Upset stomach, indigestion, diarrhea with cramping
otc_medications.notes: Will darken tongue and stool (normal)
otc_medications.contraindications: Aspirin allergy, anticoagulation, children with viral illness

otc_medications.notes: AVOID NSAIDs (ibuprofen) if stomach pain or GI bleeding suspected

otc_medications.dosage: See constipation protocol - start with bulk-forming
otc_medications.notes: Do NOT use if severe pain, vomiting, or possible obstruction

red_flags: Severe sudden onset pain (especially in older adults)
Right lower quadrant pain with fever (appendicitis)
Blood in stool (red or black tarry stools)
Unable to pass gas or stool (obstruction)
Severe pain with pulsating abdominal mass (AAA)
Pain preventing lying still or worsening with movement

emergency_911: Suspected ruptured AAA or ectopic pregnancy
Abdominal pain with shock signs (pale, clammy, rapid pulse)
urgent_care_same_day: Unable to pass gas/stool for >24 hours
Pain with urinary symptoms (flank pain, dysuria)
primary_care_24_48hrs: Need for evaluation of chronic condition

key_points: Location of pain helps narrow differential diagnosis
Sudden severe pain in older adult is emergency
Right lower quadrant pain with fever = appendicitis until proven otherwise
Peritoneal signs (guarding, rebound) indicate serious pathology
Blood in vomit or stool always requires evaluation
Keep NPO (nothing by mouth) if severe pain or possible surgery
alarm_features: Family history of GI malignancy or IBD

symptoms.description: Excess nasal drainage, clear or discolored mucus from nose

mild.characteristics: Minimal interference with activities, no other symptoms

moderate.characteristics: Interferes with sleep or daily activities, may have associated symptoms

severe.characteristics: Significant impairment, thick discolored drainage, fever, facial pain

rhinorrhea_characteristics.yellow_green: Bacterial sinusitis (if >10 days), late viral infection
rhinorrhea_characteristics.bloody: Trauma, dry air, serious pathology if persistent
rhinorrhea_characteristics.unilateral: Foreign body, CSF leak, tumor (requires evaluation)

common_causes: Medications (rhinitis medicamentosa from nasal spray overuse)

home_remedies: Saline nasal irrigation: Neti pot or saline spray 2-3 times daily
Stay well hydrated: Thins mucus secretions
Humidifier: Adds moisture to air, especially in bedroom
Steam inhalation: Hot shower or bowl of hot water, 10-15 minutes
Warm compress over sinuses
Elevate head while sleeping (2-3 pillows)
Hot tea or soup: Steam and hydration combined
Avoid allergens if allergic rhinitis
Blow nose gently: One nostril at a time to prevent ear pressure
Use soft tissues with lotion to prevent skin irritation

otc_medications.dosage: Use as often as needed throughout day
otc_medications.best_for: All types of rhinorrhea, very safe
otc_medications.notes: Use distilled, sterile, or previously boiled water in neti pots. Most effective treatment

otc_medications.dosage: Loratadine 10mg once daily, Cetirizine 10mg once daily, Fexofenadine 180mg once daily
otc_medications.notes: Less sedating than 1st generation. Take regularly for allergies, not as needed

otc_medications.dosage: Diphenhydramine 25-50mg every 4-6 hours, Chlorpheniramine 4mg every 4-6 hours
otc_medications.notes: Causes significant drowsiness - bedtime use only. Dries secretions
otc_medications.contraindications: Elderly (fall risk), glaucoma, prostate enlargement, driving/operating machinery

otc_medications.dosage: Adults: 30-60mg every 4-6 hours (max 240mg/24hrs) OR 120mg extended-release every 12 hours
otc_medications.mechanism: Sympathomimetic - causes vasoconstriction in nasal passages
otc_medications.notes: Behind pharmacy counter (not prescription). Can increase BP and heart rate. More effective than phenylephrine
otc_medications.contraindications: Uncontrolled hypertension, coronary artery disease, MAOIs, hyperthyroidism

otc_medications.best_for: Allergic rhinitis, non-allergic rhinitis - MOST EFFECTIVE for chronic rhinorrhea
otc_medications.notes: Takes 1-2 weeks for full effect. Very safe for long-term use. Aim spray toward outer wall of nose, not septum
otc_medications.contraindications: Recent nasal surgery, nasal septum ulcer, epistaxis

otc_medications.notes: Specifically targets rhinorrhea. Available OTC in some formulations

red_flags: Clear drainage from nose after head trauma (CSF leak)
Bloody drainage that is persistent or recurrent
Facial pain and fever with yellow/green discharge >10 days (bacterial sinusitis)
Swelling of face or around eyes

emergency_911: Clear fluid from nose after head trauma
Severe headache with fever and purulent discharge
urgent_care_same_day: Symptoms >10 days with no improvement (bacterial sinusitis)
High fever with thick yellow/green discharge

key_points: Most common colds last 7-10 days
Color of mucus alone doesn't indicate bacterial infection
Nasal irrigation most effective home treatment
Intranasal steroids most effective medication for chronic rhinitis
Antihistamines only help if allergic cause
Avoid overuse of nasal decongestant sprays (>3 days) - causes rebound congestion
viral_vs_bacterial: Viral: Clear or white mucus, gradual onset, peak 3-5 days then improve
Bacterial: Symptoms >10 days without improvement, OR worsening after initial improvement, OR severe symptoms (fever >39°C, purulent discharge) for 3+ consecutive days

symptoms.description: Blocked or stuffy nose, difficulty breathing through nasal passages

mild.characteristics: Can still breathe through nose with some difficulty, minimal impact

moderate.characteristics: Difficult to breathe through nose, mouth breathing common, affects sleep

severe.characteristics: Cannot breathe through nose at all, significant sleep disruption, affecting quality of life

common_causes: Rhinitis medicamentosa (rebound from decongestant spray overuse)

home_remedies: Saline nasal irrigation: Neti pot or squeeze bottle 2-3 times daily - MOST EFFECTIVE
Steam inhalation: Hot shower, facial steaming with eucalyptus oil 10-15 minutes
Humidifier: Run in bedroom overnight, keep humidity 30-50%
Stay well-hydrated: 8-10 glasses water daily - thins secretions
Elevate head while sleeping: Use 2-3 pillows or raise head of bed 30-45 degrees
Warm compress: Apply over sinuses for 5-10 minutes several times daily
Spicy foods: May temporarily open nasal passages
Avoid known allergens
Maintain clean air: HEPA filters, regular dusting
Exercise: Mild exercise can temporarily relieve congestion

otc_medications.notes: VERY EFFECTIVE but DO NOT USE >3 CONSECUTIVE DAYS - causes rebound congestion (rhinitis medicamentosa)
otc_medications.contraindications: Do not use if already have rebound congestion
otc_medications.warning: MAXIMUM 3 DAYS USE - longer causes dependence and worsening

otc_medications.notes: Less effective than oxymetazoline. Same 3-day maximum rule

otc_medications.dosage: Adults: 30-60mg every 4-6 hours (max 240mg/24hrs) OR 120mg ER every 12 hours
otc_medications.best_for: Congestion without risk of rebound, can use longer than nasal sprays
otc_medications.notes: Behind pharmacy counter. May increase blood pressure and heart rate. More effective than phenylephrine oral
otc_medications.contraindications: Severe hypertension, coronary artery disease, MAOIs, hyperthyroidism

otc_medications.notes: On shelf without ID. Recent studies show minimal effectiveness - much less effective than pseudoephedrine

otc_medications.best_for: MOST EFFECTIVE for chronic congestion, allergic rhinitis, non-allergic rhinitis
otc_medications.notes: Takes 1-2 weeks for full effect. Safe for long-term use. No rebound congestion. Aim toward outer nasal wall
otc_medications.contraindications: Active nasal bleeding, recent nasal surgery

otc_medications.notes: Only effective if allergies are cause. Cetirizine may help more with congestion than other 2nd gen

red_flags: Unilateral congestion (one side only) - may indicate structural issue or mass
Congestion with vision changes or eye swelling

emergency_911: Infant with complete nasal obstruction (can't feed)
Signs of severe infection (high fever, altered mental status)

key_points: Nasal irrigation is the safest and one of most effective treatments
Intranasal steroids are most effective for chronic congestion - but take 1-2 weeks
NEVER use nasal decongestant sprays (Afrin) for more than 3 days
Rebound congestion from spray overuse is very difficult to treat
Oral pseudoephedrine more effective than phenylephrine (Sudafed PE)
Humidity between 30-50% optimal - too high promotes mold
Chronic congestion may indicate structural issue requiring ENT evaluation
preventing_rebound_congestion: Limit nasal decongestant sprays to 3 days maximum
Use intranasal steroids for maintenance if chronic congestion
If already have rebound: stop spray (may be worse for few days), use saline and intranasal steroid
Mark calendar when starting spray to track days used
neti_pot_safety: Use only distilled, sterile, or previously boiled (then cooled) water
Never use tap water - risk of rare but serious infection
Clean and dry neti pot after each use

symptoms.description: Generalized muscle pain and soreness throughout the body

mild.characteristics: Doesn't significantly interfere with activities, similar to post-exercise soreness

moderate.characteristics: Affects daily activities, causes fatigue, difficulty with movement

severe.characteristics: Debilitating pain, unable to perform normal activities, may have other severe symptoms

common_causes: Autoimmune conditions (lupus, rheumatoid arthritis, polymyalgia rheumatica)

home_remedies: Rest adequately: Get 7-9 hours sleep, take breaks during day
Warm bath or shower: Add Epsom salts (magnesium sulfate) 2 cups to bath, soak 15-20 minutes
Heat application: Heating pad or warm compress to sore areas 15-20 minutes
Cold therapy: Ice packs if acute injury or inflammation, 15-20 minutes
Gentle stretching: Light yoga, range-of-motion exercises
Massage: Self-massage or professional massage therapy
Stay hydrated: 8-10 glasses water daily
Maintain good nutrition: Adequate protein, fruits, vegetables
Stress reduction: Meditation, deep breathing, relaxation techniques

mild.characteristics: Mild redness or small bumps, minimal itching or discomfort

moderate.characteristics: More extensive rash, moderate itching, some impact on activities

severe.description: Widespread, severe symptoms, or concerning features
severe.characteristics: Large areas affected, severe itching/pain, blistering, fever, systemic symptoms

rash_characteristics.petechial: Tiny red/purple dots that don't blanch - CONCERNING

home_remedies: Identify and avoid trigger/irritant
Cool compress: Apply to affected area 15-20 minutes
Lukewarm oatmeal bath: Colloidal oatmeal, soak 15-20 minutes
Keep area clean and dry
Wear loose, breathable cotton clothing
Avoid scratching: Trim nails, wear gloves at night if needed
Moisturize: Fragrance-free, hypoallergenic lotion after bathing
Avoid hot water: Use lukewarm water for bathing
Avoid known allergens and irritants
For contact dermatitis: Wash area immediately after exposure
Gentle, fragrance-free soaps and detergents
Stress reduction: Stress can worsen some rashes

otc_medications.dosage: Apply thin layer to affected area 2-4 times daily for up to 7 days
otc_medications.mechanism: Topical corticosteroid - reduces inflammation and itching
otc_medications.best_for: Eczema, contact dermatitis, allergic rashes, insect bites
otc_medications.notes: Don't use on face without doctor guidance. Don't use >7 days without medical advice. Avoid near eyes
otc_medications.contraindications: Active infection (bacterial, viral, fungal), acne, rosacea

otc_medications.dosage: Cetirizine 10mg daily, Loratadine 10mg daily, Diphenhydramine 25-50mg every 4-6 hours
otc_medications.notes: Diphenhydramine more sedating but works faster. 2nd generation (cetirizine, loratadine) less sedating
otc_medications.contraindications: Elderly (1st generation antihistamines increase fall risk)

otc_medications.dosage: Apply to affected area as needed
otc_medications.notes: Very safe. Pink color can stain clothing. Dries skin

otc_medications.dosage: Bath: Add to lukewarm water, soak 15-20 min. Lotion: Apply as needed
otc_medications.notes: Very gentle and safe. Good for sensitive skin

otc_medications.dosage: Apply twice daily to affected area for 2-4 weeks
otc_medications.best_for: Ringworm, jock itch, athlete's foot, yeast infections
otc_medications.notes: Continue for full course even if improves. Terbinafine (Lamisil) often most effective
otc_medications.contraindications: Don't use if not fungal (can worsen other conditions)

red_flags: ⚠️ CRITICAL: Rash with difficulty breathing or swelling (anaphylaxis)
Petechial rash (tiny red/purple dots that don't blanch) - possible meningitis
Rash with joint pain or swelling
Signs of infection: Increasing redness, warmth, pus, red streaks

emergency_911: Rash with difficulty breathing, throat swelling (anaphylaxis)
Severe pain with rapidly spreading rash
Suspected Stevens-Johnson syndrome (severe blistering after medication)
primary_care_few_days: Persistent rash not improving with OTC treatment

key_points: Most rashes are benign and self-limited
Identify and avoid triggers when possible
Avoid scratching - can lead to infection and scarring
Moisturizing is key for many skin conditions
Hydrocortisone cream safe for short-term use (<7 days)
Antihistamines most helpful for itchy, allergic rashes
Take photos to track progression
New rash after medication should be evaluated

specific_rash_tips.poison_ivy: Wash skin immediately with soap and water if exposed. Wash clothes and items that contacted plant. Rash not contagious (fluid doesn't spread it)
specific_rash_tips.eczema: Moisturize frequently (especially after bathing). Identify and avoid triggers. May need long-term management
specific_rash_tips.hives: Usually allergic. Take antihistamine. Most resolve in 24-48 hours. Chronic hives (>6 weeks) need evaluation
specific_rash_tips.fungal: Keep area clean and dry. Change socks daily. Complete full treatment course

symptoms.description: Uncomfortable sensation causing desire to scratch

mild.characteristics: Mild discomfort, doesn't affect sleep or daily activities

moderate.characteristics: Notable discomfort, some sleep disruption, affects concentration

severe.characteristics: Significant sleep disruption, skin damage from scratching, severely affects quality of life

pruritus_with_vs_without_rash.with_rash: Usually dermatological cause - eczema, psoriasis, contact dermatitis, fungal infection, scabies, etc.
pruritus_with_vs_without_rash.without_rash: May indicate systemic cause - needs evaluation. Causes include: kidney disease, liver disease, thyroid disorder, lymphoma, polycythemia vera, medications, dry skin, neuropathy

common_causes: Systemic causes: Kidney disease, liver disease, thyroid disorders, diabetes, lymphoma, iron deficiency

home_remedies: Moisturize regularly: Apply thick cream or ointment 2-3 times daily, especially after bathing
Lukewarm baths: Avoid hot water which dries skin
Oatmeal baths: Colloidal oatmeal, soak 15-20 minutes
Cool compress or ice pack: Apply to itchy area
Avoid scratching: Trim nails, wear cotton gloves at night
Pat or tap skin instead of scratching
Wear soft, breathable fabrics: Cotton preferred
Use fragrance-free, hypoallergenic products
Humidifier: Especially in winter, maintain 30-50% humidity
Avoid irritants: Harsh soaps, detergents, wool
Stress reduction: Stress can worsen itching
Keep cool: Heat worsens itching

otc_medications.dosage: Cetirizine 10mg daily, Loratadine 10mg daily, Fexofenadine 180mg daily
otc_medications.best_for: Allergic itching, hives, itching without rash
otc_medications.notes: Take regularly for best effect. Less sedating. Cetirizine may work better for itching than others

otc_medications.dosage: Diphenhydramine 25-50mg every 4-6 hours, max at bedtime
otc_medications.best_for: Severe itching, nighttime itching disrupting sleep
otc_medications.notes: Very sedating - use at bedtime. More effective for itching than 2nd generation but drowsiness limits daytime use
otc_medications.contraindications: Elderly (fall risk, confusion), glaucoma, prostate enlargement

otc_medications.dosage: Apply thin layer to itchy areas 2-4 times daily (max 7 days)
otc_medications.best_for: Localized itching from eczema, contact dermatitis, insect bites
otc_medications.notes: Works for inflammatory itching. Don't use on face without guidance. Limit use to 7 days

otc_medications.dosage: Apply to affected area as needed
otc_medications.mechanism: Calamine: Soothing, cooling. Pramoxine: Topical anesthetic
otc_medications.notes: Safe for frequent use. Calamine can dry skin. Pramoxine (in Caladryl, Gold Bond) numbs area

otc_medications.medication: Menthol or camphor creams (Gold Bond, Sarna)
otc_medications.dosage: Apply to itchy areas as needed
otc_medications.notes: Provides symptomatic relief. Can use frequently. Avoid mucous membranes

otc_medications.medication: Moisturizers - Thick creams/ointments (CeraVe, Cetaphil, Eucerin, Aquaphor)
otc_medications.dosage: Apply liberally 2-3 times daily, especially after bathing
otc_medications.mechanism: Restores skin barrier, prevents water loss
otc_medications.notes: Ointments (petroleum-based) most effective but greasy. Creams good compromise. Apply to damp skin after bathing

red_flags: Severe itching without visible rash (systemic cause)
Itching with jaundice (yellowing skin/eyes) - liver disease
Severe itching affecting sleep for prolonged period
Itching with weight loss, fever, night sweats (lymphoma)
Rapidly spreading itchy rash in household members (scabies)

emergency_911: Severe itching with signs of severe allergic reaction
primary_care_1_2_weeks: Itching without rash >2 weeks (needs evaluation for systemic causes)
Chronic persistent itching not responding to OTC treatment
Itching significantly affecting quality of life or sleep
Need for evaluation: Labs (kidney, liver, thyroid, CBC), dermatology referral if needed

key_points: Moisturizing is THE most important treatment for most itching
Apply moisturizer within 3 minutes after bathing (to damp skin)
Scratching makes itching worse - breaks itch-scratch cycle
Itching without rash may indicate internal disease
Antihistamines work best when taken regularly, not as needed
Hot water temporarily relieves itching but worsens it long-term
Many causes of itching are chronic and need ongoing management
breaking_itch_scratch_cycle: Scratching provides brief relief but damages skin and worsens itching
Apply cold compress instead of scratching
Tap or pat itchy area instead of scratching
Distraction techniques when urge to scratch arises
Address underlying cause for long-term relief
when_systemic_cause_likely: Not responding to topical treatments and antihistamines
Associated symptoms: jaundice, weight loss, fatigue
Elderly patient with new onset generalized itching
Requires workup: CBC, metabolic panel, liver function, thyroid, kidney function

symptoms.description: Redness or bloodshot appearance of the eye

mild.characteristics: Minimal discomfort, no vision changes, no discharge

moderate.characteristics: Gritty feeling, mild discharge, some irritation

severe.characteristics: Pain, vision changes, significant discharge, light sensitivity

home_remedies: Warm compress: For bacterial/viral conjunctivitis, blepharitis - 10 min, 3-4 times daily
Cold compress: For allergic conjunctivitis - 10 min as needed
Artificial tears: Lubricating eye drops, as needed throughout day
Avoid rubbing eyes: Worsens irritation, spreads infection
Remove contact lenses: Until symptoms resolve
Maintain eye hygiene: Clean eyelids gently with warm water
Avoid eye makeup: Until infection resolves
Discard old eye makeup: Replace after eye infection
Wash hands frequently: Prevent spread
Avoid sharing towels, pillows: If infectious
Stay hydrated: Helps with dry eyes
Reduce screen time: Follow 20-20-20 rule
Remove irritants: Avoid smoke, allergens

otc_medications.dosage: 1-2 drops in affected eye(s) as needed, up to 4-6 times daily
otc_medications.best_for: Dry eyes, mild irritation, computer eye strain
otc_medications.notes: Preservative-free preferred for frequent use (>4x/day). Very safe. Can use with other eye drops (wait 5 min between)

otc_medications.dosage: 1 drop in affected eye(s) twice daily
otc_medications.notes: Now OTC. Works quickly (minutes). Can use for seasonal allergies. More effective than oral antihistamines for eye allergies

otc_medications.best_for: Cosmetic redness reduction for special occasions
otc_medications.notes: DO NOT USE REGULARLY - causes rebound redness. Masks problem without treating cause. Use sparingly
otc_medications.contraindications: Glaucoma, regular use causes rebound hyperemia
otc_medications.warning: Not for routine use - can worsen redness with regular use

otc_medications.dosage: Apply small amount to lower lid at bedtime
otc_medications.best_for: Severe dry eyes, nighttime dryness, protection during sleep
otc_medications.notes: Blurs vision - use only at bedtime. More effective than drops for severe dryness

red_flags: ⚠️ Sudden vision loss or significant vision changes
Foreign body that can't be flushed out
Eye redness with contact lens wear (keratitis risk)
Eye redness not improving after 2-3 days
History of herpes simplex and eye redness

emergency_911_or_ER: Chemical exposure to eye (flush with water for 15 min, then go to ER)
urgent_care_same_day: Foreign body sensation that won't flush out
Thick discharge with swollen lids (bacterial conjunctivitis)
Contact lens wearer with red, painful eye
Eye redness with headache and light sensitivity
primary_care_1_2_days: Chronic dry eyes needing prescription treatment

key_points: Viral conjunctivitis (pink eye) very contagious - frequent handwashing essential
Most cases of viral conjunctivitis resolve on their own in 1-2 weeks
Antibiotics only help bacterial conjunctivitis, not viral
Never share eye makeup, contact lenses, or towels
Remove contact lenses if eyes red - don't wear until resolved
Subconjunctival hemorrhage (broken blood vessel) looks scary but harmless
Artificial tears are safe and effective for most mild redness
Avoid decongestant eye drops (Visine) for regular use

conjunctivitis_types.viral: Watery discharge, very contagious, often with cold symptoms. No antibiotics needed. Resolves 1-2 weeks
conjunctivitis_types.bacterial: Thick yellow/green discharge, crusted lids in morning. May need antibiotic drops. Contagious
conjunctivitis_types.allergic: Itchy, watery, both eyes affected. NOT contagious. Antihistamine drops very effective

when_antibiotics_needed: Contact lens wearer (higher risk of serious infection)

symptoms.description: Pain in or around the ear

mild.characteristics: Mild pain, no fever, hearing normal

moderate.characteristics: Moderate pain affecting activities, possible hearing changes

severe.characteristics: Intense pain, fever, drainage, severe hearing loss

common_causes: Otitis media (middle ear infection) - especially children

home_remedies: Warm compress: Apply to ear 15-20 minutes several times daily
Keep ear dry: Avoid getting water in ear, use earplugs when bathing
Chew gum: For eustachian tube dysfunction, helps equalize pressure
Rest with affected ear elevated: May reduce pressure
Avoid inserting anything into ear canal: No cotton swabs, bobby pins
Stay hydrated
Yawning or swallowing: Helps open eustachian tube
Humidity: Use humidifier if dry air contributing

otc_medications.dosage: Acetaminophen 500-1000mg every 4-6 hrs, Ibuprofen 400mg every 6-8 hrs
otc_medications.notes: Ibuprofen may be slightly more effective due to anti-inflammatory properties

otc_medications.dosage: Fill ear canal, keep in place 5-10 min, 3-4 times daily
otc_medications.notes: DO NOT USE if eardrum perforated (drainage present). Provides temporary relief only - doesn't treat infection
otc_medications.warning: Stop if ear is draining - indicates possible perforation

otc_medications.dosage: Few drops after swimming or bathing
otc_medications.mechanism: Dries ear canal, acidifies to prevent bacteria
otc_medications.best_for: PREVENTION of swimmer's ear, not treatment
otc_medications.notes: Use after water exposure if prone to swimmer's ear. Can make at home: 1:1 rubbing alcohol and white vinegar
otc_medications.contraindications: Active infection, perforated eardrum, ear tubes

red_flags: Drainage from ear (pus, blood, clear fluid)
Swelling around ear or mastoid area (behind ear)
Diabetes or immunocompromised with ear infection
Sudden severe pain that then improves (possible perforation)

emergency_911_or_ER: Severe pain with facial weakness or drooping
Ear pain after significant head trauma
Severe swelling behind ear with fever (mastoiditis)
Signs of meningitis (stiff neck, severe headache, confusion)
urgent_care_same_day: Infant or young child with ear pain and fever
Ear pain not controlled with OTC pain medication

key_points: Otitis media (middle ear infection) often follows viral URI
Most middle ear infections are viral and don't need antibiotics
Antibiotics prescribed if: Age <6 months, severe symptoms, bilateral in young child, persistent >48-72 hours
Never put objects in ear canal - including cotton swabs
Ear drops don't work for middle ear infections (behind eardrum)
Swimmer's ear (outer ear infection) very different from middle ear infection
Don't use ear drops if drainage present - may indicate perforation

otitis_media_vs_externa.otitis_media: Middle ear infection behind eardrum. Often after cold. Ear looks red when examined. Needs oral antibiotics if bacterial. Ear drops don't help
otitis_media_vs_externa.otitis_externa: Outer ear canal infection (swimmer's ear). Pain with pulling on ear or pressing tragus. Often after water exposure. Needs antibiotic ear drops

prevention.otitis_media: Breastfeeding infants, avoid secondhand smoke, vaccinations up to date, avoid bottle propping
prevention.otitis_externa: Dry ears after swimming, use prevention drops if prone, avoid cotton swabs, don't remove all earwax (it's protective)

symptoms.description: Pain in or around a tooth

mild.characteristics: Brief pain with hot/cold, no spontaneous pain

moderate.characteristics: Persistent discomfort, pain with chewing, some spontaneous pain

severe.characteristics: Constant severe pain, swelling, fever, difficulty eating/sleeping

common_causes: Sinus infection (referred pain to upper teeth)

home_remedies: Rinse with warm salt water: 1/2 tsp salt in 8oz warm water, swish 30 sec, repeat every 2-3 hours
Cold compress: Apply to cheek over painful area 15-20 min
Elevate head when sleeping: May reduce pressure and pain
Clove oil: Apply small amount to cotton ball, place near affected tooth (natural numbing agent)
Avoid triggers: Very hot, cold, or sweet foods and beverages
Soft foods: Avoid chewing on affected side
Maintain oral hygiene: Gentle brushing and flossing (don't skip painful area)
Avoid alcohol and smoking: Can worsen pain and delay healing

otc_medications.notes: Superior to acetaminophen for dental pain. Take with food. Can alternate with acetaminophen for severe pain
otc_medications.contraindications: GI ulcers, kidney disease, bleeding disorders

otc_medications.best_for: Alternative if NSAIDs contraindicated, or for combination with ibuprofen
otc_medications.notes: Can alternate with ibuprofen every 3 hours for severe pain (e.g., ibuprofen at 9am, acetaminophen at noon, ibuprofen at 3pm)

otc_medications.dosage: Apply small amount directly to affected tooth/gum as needed (max 4 times daily)
otc_medications.best_for: Temporary relief while waiting for dental appointment
otc_medications.notes: Provides 15-20 min relief. Don't swallow. Not for children <2 years. TEMPORARY ONLY
otc_medications.warning: Does NOT treat underlying problem - dental evaluation needed

otc_medications.dosage: Apply tiny amount to cotton ball, hold near tooth, or dilute 1-2 drops in carrier oil
otc_medications.notes: Traditional remedy with some evidence. Use sparingly - can irritate gums. Strong taste
otc_medications.contraindications: Don't use undiluted, can damage tissues

red_flags: Severe pain not controlled by OTC medications
Facial swelling or swelling in neck
Severe pain radiating to jaw, ear, or neck
Recent dental procedure with worsening pain (dry socket)
Diabetes or immunocompromised with dental infection

emergency_911_or_ER: Severe facial swelling affecting eye or extending to neck
High fever with severe dental pain and swelling
Suspected Ludwig's angina (floor of mouth swelling)
urgent_dental_care_same_day: Broken tooth with exposed nerve (extreme pain)
Knocked-out permanent tooth (bring tooth in milk, see dentist within 30 min if possible)
Dry socket (severe pain 3-4 days after extraction)
dental_appointment_1_3_days: Visible cavity or dark spot on tooth
Any toothache should be evaluated - underlying problem won't resolve without treatment

key_points: Toothache indicates a problem that needs dental treatment
Pain medication provides temporary relief but doesn't fix the problem
Ibuprofen most effective OTC pain reliever for dental pain
Dental infections can become serious - don't delay treatment
Abscess can spread to neck, brain - potentially life-threatening
Knocked-out permanent tooth: Put back in socket if possible or store in milk, see dentist ASAP
Regular dental checkups prevent most dental emergencies

emergency_tooth_care.knocked_out_tooth: Handle by crown not root. Rinse gently if dirty. Try to reinsert in socket. If not possible, store in milk or between cheek and gum. See dentist within 30 minutes
emergency_tooth_care.broken_tooth: Rinse mouth, save pieces, cold compress for swelling, see dentist ASAP
emergency_tooth_care.object_stuck_between_teeth: Try floss gently. Do NOT use sharp objects. See dentist if can't remove

prevention: Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste
Address teeth grinding (bruxism) with night guard if needed

symptoms.description: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in tissues causing puffiness or enlargement

mild.description: Slight puffiness, mild indentation with pressure
mild.characteristics: Cosmetic concern, minimal discomfort, doesn't affect function

moderate.characteristics: Affects comfort, some functional limitation, tight feeling

severe.description: Severe swelling, may have skin changes
severe.characteristics: Significant functional impairment, skin taut and shiny, possible skin breakdown

edema_types.localized: One area - suggests local cause (injury, infection, DVT, lymphatic obstruction)
edema_types.generalized: Multiple areas or entire body - suggests systemic cause (heart, kidney, liver disease)
edema_types.unilateral_leg: ONE leg swollen - DVT until proven otherwise
edema_types.bilateral_legs: Both legs - venous insufficiency, heart failure, medications
edema_types.facial: May indicate kidney disease, allergic reaction, or superior vena cava syndrome
edema_types.abdominal: Ascites - liver disease, cancer, heart failure

common_causes: Medications (calcium channel blockers, NSAIDs, corticosteroids, hormones)

home_remedies: Elevate affected area: Above heart level for 30 min, 3-4 times daily
Reduce salt intake: <2300mg sodium daily (1500mg if heart/kidney disease)
Stay hydrated: Paradoxically, dehydration can worsen edema
Regular movement: Avoid prolonged sitting/standing, walk around every hour
Compression stockings: 15-20 mmHg for mild edema (consult doctor for higher compression)
Exercise regularly: Promotes circulation, especially leg exercises
Massage: Gentle massage toward heart may help (lymphatic drainage)
Avoid tight clothing: Especially around ankles, waist
Maintain healthy weight: Obesity worsens edema
Elevate legs when sitting: Use footstool
Sleep with legs elevated: Pillows under ankles

otc_medications.medication: Note: Edema requires treating underlying cause
otc_medications.notes: OTC diuretics (water pills) NOT recommended without medical supervision. Can cause dangerous electrolyte imbalances. Focus on lifestyle modifications and treating underlying cause
otc_medications.warning: Do NOT take OTC diuretics without doctor supervision

otc_medications.dosage: Wear during day, remove at night
otc_medications.best_for: Mild leg edema from prolonged standing, venous insufficiency, pregnancy
otc_medications.notes: Put on in morning before getting out of bed. Proper fit important. Higher compression requires prescription

red_flags: CRITICAL: Unilateral leg swelling with pain (DVT - blood clot)
Sudden swelling of face, lips, tongue (anaphylaxis)
Shortness of breath with leg swelling (heart failure, PE)
Swelling after long flight or immobility (DVT risk)
Rapid weight gain (>2-3 lbs in a day or 5 lbs in a week)
Swelling with severe headache, vision changes (preeclampsia in pregnancy)

emergency_911: Sudden facial, lip, or tongue swelling with difficulty breathing (anaphylaxis)
Chest pain or severe shortness of breath with leg swelling
One swollen painful leg (especially if calf pain, warmth, redness) - DVT
Pregnant woman with sudden swelling and headache (preeclampsia)
urgent_care_same_day: Significant shortness of breath with swelling
primary_care_1_2_weeks: Need for evaluation: Cardiac echo, kidney function, liver function, venous duplex

key_points: Edema is a symptom, not a diagnosis - needs evaluation for underlying cause
Unilateral (one-sided) leg swelling is DVT until proven otherwise
Elevation above heart level is the most effective home treatment
Salt restriction helps reduce fluid retention
Many common medications cause edema (calcium channel blockers, NSAIDs)
Compression stockings are very effective for venous edema
Don't take diuretics without medical supervision
dvt_warning_signs: Recent surgery, long flight, or prolonged immobility
DVT is a medical emergency - can lead to pulmonary embolism (PE)
when_edema_indicates_serious_disease: Bilateral leg edema with shortness of breath (heart failure)
Requires urgent medical evaluation and treatment of underlying condition
